chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about fasting the whole time, so he disliked it and said: There is no problem if one were to fast for one day and break (not fast) for one day.

key_terms.صَوْمِ الدَّهْرِ: Continuous fasting (fasting every day without break)
key_terms.فَكَرِهَهُ: He disliked it (expressing mild disapproval or dislike of the practice)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on fasting continuously every day without breaking the fast?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Samaanah reports asking Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about *Sawm al-Dahr* (continuous fasting), to which the Imam expressed dislike (*karah*) and recommended the Sunnah of fasting one day and breaking the next. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly preference for moderation (*wasatiyyah*) over extreme asceticism, aligning with the Prophet’s practice of fasting Dawud (AS), thereby preventing physical exhaustion and maintaining spiritual consistency.
